takeaway: The turn to trade winds is here. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has a mostly sunny day on the North Pacific, with only a low chance of an isolated afternoon shower on the Nicoya Peninsula and Nicoya near 34°C. Northeast breezes hold over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica for the next two weeks, and IMN now expects the dry season to settle in on the North Pacific during the week of Oct 25–Nov 1. For surf, it's offshore today and every day through Sunday, with a long-period south-southwest swell (about 18 seconds today). This is the best wind-and-swell combo in a while. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Wed–Fri, Oct 21–23)
periods.pattern: IMN's Wednesday forecast for the North Pacific is partly cloudy in the morning and only partly cloudy in the afternoon, with a possible isolated downpour on the peninsula. It says the chance is low. Tonight stays partly cloudy, with moderate wind in the mountains. Nicoya's high is about 34°C and the low about 23°C. IMN says the tropical shower band is still adding some moisture, but the storms today favor the Central and South Pacific, the Northern Zone, and the Caribbean mountains, not Nicoya. The models disagree a little on rain near Nosara. The American averages show a wetter 24 hours ending this evening (about an inch, much of it from last night's coastal showers), while the European averages show only about 3–8 mm (a quarter inch or less). Thursday and Friday look light, mostly a few millimeters, with the European average up to about 10 mm (0.4 inch) on Friday.
periods.implications: Good outdoor days. Expect sun, heat around 34°C, and a breeze. A stray afternoon shower is possible but unlikely on most days. Mornings are still the coolest time for anything active.
periods.confidence: High on the drier, breezier turn. Moderate on whether a passing shower clips Nosara Friday.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sat–Tue, Oct 24–27)
periods.pattern: All the ensemble averages keep a steady northeast-to-east breeze across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica, with the heaviest rain on the Caribbean side. IMN's weekly outlook still expects the season's first cold push to reach the northern Caribbean this weekend. It won't hit Costa Rica directly, but it brings drier air and occasional moderate winds to the North Pacific. One thing to know: the European models now show light passing showers near the peninsula Saturday through Monday, around a third of an inch (8–10 mm) on some days. The American and AI-based European averages are drier, mostly 2–5 mm a day.
periods.implications: Mostly a good stretch for the beach and outdoor plans: sunny, breezy, less humid. Keep a light rain layer handy in case a brief shower drifts off the hills in the afternoon.
periods.confidence: Moderate-high on breezy and mostly dry. Moderate on how many brief showers sneak in.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Wed Oct 28 – Wed Nov 4)
periods.pattern: The trades keep blowing over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica into early November, and two of the models show high pressure building over southern Mexico and Guatemala around Oct 31, which usually strengthens the breeze through the Papagayo gap. IMN's updated long-range outlook (now through Nov 15) calls for dry conditions on the North Pacific, says the dry season should become established there the week of Oct 25–Nov 1, and calls for very dry weather Nov 9–15. It sees low odds of an extreme rain event (about 10%). The model averages hint that the rain band to the south edges closer in early November, with near-Nosara daily amounts creeping up to about 10 mm, and the European average wetter by Nov 4. That's the far end of the forecast and runs against IMN's dry call.
periods.implications: Good odds of a mostly dry, sunny, breezy end to October. Early November is less certain, so don't lock in a big outdoor event on Nov 3–4 based on this yet.
periods.confidence: Moderate-high on a dry end to October. Low on the early-November details.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades, offshore at Nosara, every day from today through at least Sunday. This is a firm, steady offshore pattern, not just a light morning breeze.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 2:48 a.m. PDT Wednesday, 3:48 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds at 10–15 knots today, which is offshore here. Tonight and Thursday it's northeast to east 15–20 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo and northeast 10–15 knots elsewhere. Thursday night is north to northeast 10–15. Friday is northeast 10–15, Saturday northeast to east 10–15, and Sunday northeast to east 15–20 in the gulf with northeast around 10 elsewhere. The forecasters say the Papagayo winds will pulse to fresh each night. Swell: a long-period pulse is already in. South to southwest 5–7 feet at 18 seconds today, 4–6 feet at 17 seconds tonight, back to 5–7 feet at 17 seconds Thursday, then 4–6 feet at 14 seconds Friday and Saturday and 3–5 feet at 13 seconds Sunday. Nicaragua: every model keeps solid easterly trades over Nicaragua the whole two weeks, so Nicaragua should be offshore all day most days. That's a strong sign of good wind for Nosara mornings. Nosara sits at the edge of the stronger breeze, though, so on the lighter days an afternoon sea breeze can still put some texture on it. Don't count on all-day offshore here every day.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today: offshore all day is possible, and the 18-second swell makes it worth getting out early. Thursday morning: likely the pick of the week, with firmer northeast wind and the swell back up to 5–7 feet at 17 seconds. Friday and Saturday mornings: clean offshore, with a bit smaller, shorter-period swell. Sunday morning: still offshore, but the swell is fading to 3–5 feet. With long-period swell and offshore wind, the sets will be bigger and more spread out than the average height suggests, so pick your spot carefully.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore through Sunday from the marine forecast. High on the swell timing through Thursday. Moderate on how late into each afternoon the offshore holds.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, low. Nothing established, and nothing is building toward a prolonged-rain setup.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: No window stands out in the next 10 days. The only loose hint is the rain band edging closer around Nov 2–4 in some models.
gyreWatch.supporting: IMN says the tropical shower band is still nearby and adding moisture. The European models show light showers near the peninsula Saturday through Monday, and the model averages creep near-Nosara rain up to about 10 mm a day in early November, with the European average wetter by Nov 4.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model shows a broad, slow-spinning low near Costa Rica. All of them keep northeast-to-east trades over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica through early November, which is the opposite of the steady days-long Pacific wind a prolonged soak needs. The low that two models draw near northern Costa Rica around Oct 31 sits under strong trades with high pressure to the north, which is a gap-wind pattern, not a rain gyre. IMN expects the dry season to set in on the North Pacific by Nov 1 and sees no extreme events Oct 26–Nov 1. The hurricane center's system south of Mexico is about to become a tropical depression but is moving west, away from us. Nothing is expected in the Caribbean. The U.S. tropics outlook (updated Oct 20) expects below-normal rain over the Caribbean Sea and doesn't mention a Central American gyre.

whatChanged: The offshore wind showed up on schedule, and the marine forecast now keeps it going through Sunday, with Sunday's gulf winds picking back up to 15–20 knots. The long-period swell arrived sooner than expected: it's 18 seconds today instead of the 14 seconds forecast yesterday, and Thursday holds 5–7 feet at 17 seconds. IMN cut today's rain chance on Nicoya to a low chance of an isolated shower. IMN's long-range outlook was updated and now runs through Nov 15. It names the week of Oct 25–Nov 1 as when the dry season should take hold on the North Pacific. The European models are a bit wetter than yesterday for Saturday to Monday (light showers, around a third of an inch on some days), and the models now hint at a wetter early November. The hurricane center's system south of Mexico went from 90% to near 100% and should become a depression today, still heading away. The U.S. tropics outlook updated on Oct 20 and expects a drier Caribbean.
practical: Today: surf the morning (or longer) in offshore wind and an 18-second swell, then expect a hot, mostly sunny afternoon around 34°C. Thursday: probably the best surf morning of the week. Friday through the weekend: good for beach days and outdoor plans, breezy and less humid; carry a light layer for a possible brief shower Saturday to Monday. Big long-period sets mean stronger currents, so watch for rips. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
